key_insight: The paper proposes a self-evolving, expert-in-the-loop annotation framework that uses LLM assistance plus expert review to create explainable, DSM-5-TR-aligned depression symptom labels.
clinical_relevance: It aims to improve the transparency, consistency, and auditability of mental health datasets used for research and downstream AI, rather than to diagnose patients.
method: Select candidate evidence from text records
Analyze symptoms against DSM-5-TR criteria at the criterion level
Synthesize case-level labels, severity, reasoning traces, and edit histories with Example Memory and Reflection Memory
evidence_signal: A pilot study on expert-reviewed samples reported better annotation consistency and explainability with less manual revision effort, while broader multi-cycle evaluation is still future work.
watch_item: Because the framework relies on expert feedback and has not yet been fully tested across multiple feedback cycles, its scalability and robustness in diverse settings remain unproven.
paper_title: Self-Evolving Human-Centered Framework for Explainable Depression Symptom Annotation
